stem:
Carbon-15 (¹⁵₆C) is an isotope of carbon that undergoes radioactive decay to nitrogen-15 (¹⁵₇N), which is a stable isotope of nitrogen.

Radioactive decay is both a random and a spontaneous process.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A small sample of carbon-15 decays. The mass *M* of carbon-15 in the sample decreases with time *t*.

Fig. 10.1 shows the variation with *t* of the value of ln (*M* / 10⁻¹⁶ g).

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: State how Fig. 10.1 demonstrates that radioactive decay is random.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 10.1, draw the straight line of best fit.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the decay constant *λ* of carbon-15 is given by the magnitude of the gradient of your line in (b)(ii).

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use your line in (b)(ii) to determine *λ*. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(iv) to calculate the half-life of carbon-15.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The equation for the decay of carbon-15 can be written as

¹⁵₆C → ¹⁵₇N + ⁰₋₁β + ⁰₀ν̄.

State and explain how the mass of the products of the decay must compare with the mass of the carbon-15 nucleus.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A graph of ln (M / 10⁻¹⁶ g) against t / s, showing a jagged curve that decreases over time.
